Research notes (as of Mon, Oct 12, 2026):

Whether pineapple on pizza is "ok" is a matter of taste. The search results contain no rule or safety issue against it. They only show how people are split.

- **YouGov poll, March 2023:** 22% of Americans love pineapple on pizza, 37% like it, 18% dislike it and 19% hate it. The sample was 1,000 U.S. adult citizens. By this poll, a majority (about 59%) like or love it.
- **Older YouGov Omnibus survey, 2019:** 12% of Americans who eat pizza say pineapple is one of their top three favorite toppings. 24% say it is one of their least favorite. It is more popular in the western US (17%) and among ages 18–34 (15%). Northeasterners (28%) and people 55 and older (28%) are the most likely to rank it among their least favorite.
- **Slice app survey, 2017:** 54% of respondents said pineapple does not belong on pizza. That left 46% who approved.
- **Mashed poll of about 32,000 people worldwide:** About 11% chose pineapple as their go-to topping. Pepperoni won with 51%.
- **Other toppings:** Pineapple is not the most disliked topping. A 2019 YouGov poll found Americans consider anchovies and eggplant more disgusting than pineapple.
- **Origin:** Hawaiian pizza (ham and pineapple) was invented in Canada in the 1960s. Wikipedia cites a CBC News obituary for its inventor, Sam Panopoulos.

The results show no consensus. Polls disagree depending on the wording and the year. The newest poll found, from 2023, leans favorable.
